findings.title: MSK cluster without logging
findings.description: Hygiene: MSK clusters should enable broker logging to CloudWatch, S3 or Firehose. Add a logging_info block.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: MSK cluster without per-topic enhanced monitoring
findings.description: An MSK cluster whose enhanced_monitoring is not PER_TOPIC_PER_BROKER emits only coarse cluster metrics, hiding per-topic anomalies that signal misuse or exfiltration. Enable PER_TOPIC_PER_BROKER monitoring.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: MSK cluster with fewer than three broker nodes
findings.description: An MSK cluster with number_of_broker_nodes below 3 cannot sustain a broker failure without losing partition availability, and single-AZ deployments concentrate blast radius. Run at least three brokers spread across availability zones.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
